author: Rinehart
text:
Since your SL got hit. I'm wondering if you have worked backwards to
see why it got hit? Where should your SL have been to be safe(r)?

author: einrikr
text:
Good question, didn't do that yet but now I have.

Rookie mistake I made here, Rinehart!

Edit: and I was too quick to press "submit" on this post.

I think, had I put my SL above the MPL of this kink in particular, it would've filled my order and not hit the SL.

author: Rinehart
text:
Good job. You got it.

When we draw our FL, you can play the FTB and you can play the MPL.
When you play the MPL, you have to ask yourself...."What is this MPL
reacting to?"

Staurum is the one that has brought this up to me multiple times and
helped reinforce the idea....although I still mess it up sometimes, lol.

That little extra cushion has saved me many times!

author: einrikr
text:
Thanks a million for making me look into it Rinehart!

And really nice to hear that what I'm saying is correct, haha.

I can imagine that we'll make this mistake a few more times, yes ;-) But
 from now on, it's something I'll have on top of mind and that helps a
lot.

Thanks again!

author: einrikr
text:
Alright. This is a nice one.

At first I thought that my order wasn't filled. It wasn't, that's for
sure, but I kept on looking into it. The order was in a good place, I
reckon, nicely at the border of a PAZ so who wouldn't want to trade
here. I figured it'd have a nice reaction, although it wasn't the
prettiest trade in the first place.

Then:

This happened. I got stopped out, again. Decided to see why and figured
that it stopped at the MPL of this LFL. Again. So first of all, there's a
 good lesson for me here.

But... while looking at the reaction, to see where it'd end, I saw price
 shooting up, then it had some sort of flash crash, engulfed the LFL
here, and look what reaction this is giving! Now, I'm not in this trade
of course, since I got stopped, but this is very interesting I'd say! Am
 I being presented with a DM here?

author: Ifmyante
text: I say yes, and it was very clever!

author: moneydeep
text:
I am new here but I would like to add what i see.

As IF always says do top down analysis. You can see in H1 that where you
 were entering is the 2nd touch and not the first in that area so clean
orders are lower below towards the MPL of the flag. IT has already taken
 those orders and therefore spike it lower where their pending orders
are.

author: einrikr
text:
Haha thanks guys! New or not, any views on the matter are very welcome and it was a good one Moneydeep, thanks.

And IF, the way you've drawn it seems very clever indeed! Almost expectable, I have to shamefully admit.

Biggest lesson in all this: KEEP LOOKING LEFT!

See the big picture.

author: einrikr
text:
I've taken a break from trading and learning for a while, to process everything I've learned.

The one thing that I notice is that I keep either having trades or trade
 opps in the wrong kind of places or they give minimum result. Or
stoploss gets hit.

I think my understanding of Flag Limits is not up to par so I am going
to focus on that. I do think that I get the basic understanding of "the
complete picture" and looking at other peoples trades I tend to
understand why they took trades on those places but when I try to do it
myself, it goes wrong.

For now, I will focus on FL's. I'll be marking them, marking what
reactions they have, try to understand what to expect and why and post
any questions I have in my FL topic and I hope that that will give me
more insight and understanding of the matter. After that, I'll focus on
other stuff and take it step by step. I've been trying to grasp all
concept at once and there are some bright moments that I do get it but they are scarce. It's feels more like I had some luck with those trades. Rather than réally know what I'm doing.

So, taking some time of is working for me I think, and now I'll get back on that horse!

author: Ifmyante
text:
Regular time off is a vital part of learning this stuff.

Well done you

author: einrikr
text:
Only 3R but I consider this learning on the go. In the end, I think
this trade is based on the right foundations. TP was rather conservative
 but there's nothing wrong with that. I wanted a TP at a place I'd be
sure of price reaching it.

Marked in this screenshot, you see what entry point I figured was best
after getting in the trade. If I figured that out before, it would be
25R but I didn't

My SL placement is good in this trade, that's something I've struggled with in the past so I'm glad I got that right.

Happy with it!

And onwards!

author: einrikr

 great way of learning, and it's basically in the right spot as well.
Just needs some fine tuning but that's part of the fun!

author: einrikr
text:
Tried a CPAZ, with good result! About 6,5R it was.

I was watching this pair still and spotted price entering a CPAZ and
entered manually. I wanted to see price pierce through the PCP before
entering. My plan was to look how far up it would go and saw that it
engulfed the tip of the CP. I had a TP setup at the upper edge of the CP
 so nice profit. Price turned around almost immediately, so quite
satisfied with this as well!

In the process, this has taught me that I could've easily held my previous position or part of it, to make it a nice 55R trade.

How would you setup a PO for these kinds of trades though? I wouldn't be
 comfortable setting it up like this... If I would've done that on this
trade, I'd get stopped out... Or have I just marked the lower level
wrong?
